scenario: Lena broke her 12-month lease and moved out on August 1 with four months remaining. The unit sat empty and was not re-rented for those four months. The landlord now demands four months of rent from Lena. The landlord listed the unit on a major rental website the day after Lena left.
policy: A tenant who breaks a fixed-term lease early is liable for rent until the unit is re-rented, but the landlord has a duty to mitigate by making reasonable efforts to re-rent. If the landlord fails to make reasonable efforts to re-rent, the tenant's liability stops on the date the tenant vacated.
